about: Claims from OG's voice comms (Maga's streams), paraphrased (never the transcript: public repo). Each claim: approximate match time (the transcripts have no timestamps; t is set from the anchor named, else null), kind (plan, read, call, reason, prediction, diagnosis, technique), the speaker's role where clear, the claim, tactics ids, the variable it suggests (comms_vars.py), and the engine's check: agrees, disagrees, partly, or can't measure, with the evidence. OG played as tag ohno in September 2026. Speakers: Maga (mesmer or elementalist), Brock (8 monk), Love (7 monk), Mo = No Monk (prot), Zinc = Zynkh (mesmer, dervish or elementalist), Joe = God Said Trap (warrior), Private (ranger, warrior or elementalist), the Rit = Demigod Aeneas (ritualist), Holy = Holye, Enigma = Enigma Og (monk), Ralph, Bago. Vocabulary (Denning): footies = footmen (base NPCs, not pit NPCs); portal = the Isle of Solitude mechanic; Ellie = elementalist; derve = dervish; writ or rit = ritualist; para = paragon; DP = death penalty; 28 = the 28:00 Lord damage decision.
vocabulary_open: lock or gate control (Isle of Weeping Stone: whether gates are a map mechanic the replay records)
Entourage (said in [xxx v ohno] late game)
the jump (said in [ohno v Fun]: a teleport, possibly the portal)

77206c78-5eb2-5a36-aa45-8e0168e624df.result: OG won at about 9:00 (Crew 17 deaths, OG 0)
77206c78-5eb2-5a36-aa45-8e0168e624df.alignment: Crew 8 Monk death 1:24 (the call to kill the lone monk at stand), first knight 1:45, boosts 3:52 and 5:52, OG's push 4:15 to 4:30, wipes 7:05 and 8:27

claims.claim: If the enemy shows four at the back, one goes to split with a monk so the rest can push hard.

check.evidence: OG split Air Ele, Fire Ele and 8 Monk from 0:14 to 2:27; Crew lost two archers (0:37, 1:13) and a knight (1:45).

claims.claim: Only one monk is at the stand, so three of us can kill it.

check.evidence: Crew 8 Monk died at 1:24 on the backside (5v5); Crew's Warrior followed at 1:48.

claims.claim: Don't converge yet: take more death penalty off them first, get a backup flag instead.

check.evidence: OG waited; Crew Paragon died at 2:41 on the backside; OG boosted at 3:52 before committing.

claims.claim: They are turtling; we have gone to 28 twice already, take this boost and then fight.

check.evidence: The turtle measure finds no turtle for Crew: Crew had deaths in the two minutes before, so the measure reads players back in base after dying, not a turtle. Question for Denning: does a team that keeps resurrecting in base and staying there count as turtling?

claims.claim: We go now, push in and spread out (said after the second boost was close).

check.evidence: Fight from 4:15 converted: Crew Paragon and Stand Mes died at 4:30 in their base; Crew lost a knight (4:30) and two archers (4:42, 5:17).

claims.claim: Double (even triple) Shatter Enchantment on the spike target kills.

check.evidence: Across 546 spikes in 61 matches, a strip on the target as the spike lands did not change the kill rate (33% with, 35% without; interval crosses zero). In this match it may still have mattered: see the question for Denning.

claims.claim: Merge (everyone together) and end it; the merge ended the game much earlier.

check.evidence: Crew wiped at 7:05 and 8:27 in its own base and pit; across 61 matches, groups of 7+ in the enemy pit or base killed in 49% of phases against 19% for 3 to 6, and lost players slightly less often.

c553716d-a00b-5bff-ac49-6bfc480c5ca9.result: OG won at about 27:40 (One wiped at the end; OG 5 deaths, One 9)
c553716d-a00b-5bff-ac49-6bfc480c5ca9.alignment: One Warrior 0:57 (the first kill at stand), One 7 Monk 6:08 and Warrior 6:25 ('solo monk again', 'we just killed their warrior'), OG dervish deaths 10:33 and 10:55 in One's base, bodyguard 23:32 and knight 23:42, One's wipe 26:46 to 27:38

claims.claim: Against double paragon, split: warrior, ranger and the 8 monk are strong on a split.

check.evidence: OG split Hammer, Ranger and 8 Monk at 0:25, 1:53 and 3:27; One lost an archer (1:00) and a knight (2:42).

claims.claim: Always keep a prot plus a monk on one side and the Rit plus a monk on the other.

check.evidence: Across 61 matches, groups of 2+ with no healer lost a player in 23% of phases against 11% with one, same local numbers (interval 5 to 17 points).

claims.claim: Five at their main with a solo monk; two monks went back for our split.

check.evidence: One's Warrior died at the stand at 0:57 (5v5). But across 61 matches a group with one healer lost players no more often than one with two at the same numbers (11.3% and 11.2%): 'solo monk' alone does not mark a kill.

claims.claim: We are on the solo monk again; we just killed their warrior.

check.evidence: One 7 Monk died at 6:08 on the backside (4v4), One Warrior at 6:25 in its own base.

claims.claim: We are boosting, so we can afford to die for NPCs.

check.evidence: OG's dervish died twice in One's base (10:33, 10:55) after the boost at 9:56; One lost one archer (10:10). Whether a death costs less while boosted is not measured yet (values.py splits deaths by role and build, not by morale).

claims.claim: They are turtling: we have to make a play; if they get a kill it may break the turtle; they can't do Lord damage.

check.evidence: The turtle measure finds One with 75%+ of its players at home for a minute or more at 9:25, 13:25, 15:30, 21:05 and 23:10. Across 61 matches, teams that turtled won 3 of 13 times.

claims.claim: Use the stairs and walls: their paragons can't hit us there.

check.evidence: No line of sight or terrain in the replay data.

claims.claim: The archer at their back is a pit NPC: Private takes it from behind while the rest hold the knight; the bodyguard too.

check.evidence: One lost its bodyguard at 23:32 and a knight at 23:42 to OG's Ranger and Ritualist split.

claims.claim: For 28: defend with the mesmer and Private, push with both melees, the Rit and the 8 monk; the infuse monk stays in base or they spike it.

check.evidence: OG split Hammer, AoB Derv, Ritualist and 8 Monk at 25:59 and 27:15; One's 4-player split took one archer (25:19) and a knight (26:44).

claims.claim: They can't do Lord damage; if we don't wipe, it's GG. Don't chase out, let them sit and regenerate.

check.evidence: The win model (never trained on this match) gave OG 98% at 26:00 and 99% at 26:30, led by the morale difference late, team strength, knights and Lord health. One wiped from 26:46.

claims.claim: Keep doing the portal loop (port in and out).

check.evidence: The portal measure finds only 2 jumps for OG and 9 for One in this match, so the loop may be walking rather than porting. Question for Denning.

a0d60daa-0700-5a31-a1f5-495c0db986df.alignment: OG 8 Monk 7:20 and Ritualist 7:34 ('we are going to lose our pit'), knight 7:47, archers 7:53 and 8:08, OG 7 Monk 11:48 and 12:10, bodyguard 14:28, OG wipe 14:53

claims.claim: Against their double split (an Ele with Return), send four plus the 8 monk out the back; this way we don't lose footmen and our damage protects our one monk.

check.evidence: NwAy split with a dervish from 0:50 and with its full team from 5:00; footmen are not pit NPCs and the engine does not track them yet, so the footmen half of the plan can't be checked.

claims.claim: We have no crowd control (no strong knockdowns or snares) and no movement control; it will probably go to 28 if we don't mess up.

check.evidence: OG's knockdowns: one Hundred Blades warrior and no hammer; NwAy capped 2 to 8 s after every OG capture from 2:10 to 6:44 while OG took 64 to 75 s each time (flag cycles). OG was behind on flags all early game.

claims.claim: Never lose gate (lock) control; one Ele running through us should not cost it.

check.evidence: No gate state in the replay data. Question for Denning: is gate control a map mechanic on Weeping Stone?

claims.claim: We are going to lose our pit; they get one knight, maybe not the other.

check.evidence: OG 8 Monk died at 7:20 on the backside (5v4), the Ritualist at 7:34 in OG's pit; OG lost a knight (7:47) and two archers (7:53, 8:08).

claims.claim: It is after time: it's a race, we have to commit now.

check.evidence: OG lost its bodyguard at 14:28 and wiped at 14:53; the res at 14:00 had just passed.

29aad8d4-e585-5b0a-af7d-93527a333d2b.alignment: xxx's four-player split 0:28 (double Ele split), OG wipe 12:55 to 13:21 and two knights 13:48, OG Mesmer, Hammer and 8 Monk 17:03 to 17:49, OG wipe in xxx's pit 27:05 to 27:37

claims.claim: It is a double Ele split (Ele monks, no Return).

check.evidence: xxx split Fire Ele, Air Ele, Ritualist and 8 Monk from 0:28 to 1:55.

claims.claim: We don't have the damage to hold the footmen; it's fine to lose them.

check.evidence: Footmen are not tracked yet.

claims.claim: Our plan was fine but we got caught: when the second Ele joined, we should have disengaged at once.

check.evidence: OG lost the fight at 12:55 on the push side (4v5): 7 Monk, Prot and AoB Derv died by 13:21, then two knights and an archer (13:48 to 13:51).

claims.claim: Defend with two monks and double run flags with Zinc until we are up on flags.

check.evidence: From 14:39 OG's Air Ele capped 16 to 40 s after each xxx capture (earlier OG took 67 to 141 s).

claims.claim: Our melee can out-damage their Eles on the Lord; we go at about 27.

check.evidence: The win model gave OG 45% at 26:00; OG wiped in xxx's pit from 27:05 (9% at 27:00). OG's Lord damage push failed against a full pit.

claims.claim: Maybe the Rit should have joined us when they sent the Eles back; no, at the end you need the Rit in base.

check.evidence: A counterfactual: the usual play needs more late-game pushes with and without a ritualist defending to compare.

1cb73c20-1b06-5b7b-a728-25c7640f8a84.result: OG won at about 25:50 (OG 2 deaths, Fun 8)
1cb73c20-1b06-5b7b-a728-25c7640f8a84.alignment: OG's two-Ele split from 0:34 and Fun's pit losses (knights 3:53 and 4:03, bodyguard 4:35, 'only one archer left'), Fun wipes 16:05 and 25:18

claims.claim: It's the invoke spike (lightning).

check.evidence: Fun ran six elementalists with Invoke Lightning and Chain Lightning.

claims.claim: Send our Eles into their base and fight the rest in ours; a full split makes their spike weaker (more targets to choose from).

claims.claim: Stay spread out as we go through.

check.evidence: Across 61 matches, players with an ally within 150 died slightly less often, not more; against teams with 2+ elementalists the difference is unclear. Deaths are the wrong outcome for this claim: area damage taken is the right one (to build).

claims.claim: The trick: pretend to collapse to our footmen, then port back into their base; every rotation does Lord damage.

check.evidence: The portal measure finds 36 jumps for OG and 59 for Fun. Lord damage per rotation is not yet tied to the jumps.

claims.claim: They will wait for 26 and make one attempt on the Lord; if we don't lose the stand team we are good on 28 damage.

check.evidence: Fun pushed and wiped from 25:18; OG won.

claims.claim: Does Aura of Faith reduce Lord damage?

check.evidence: A mechanics question for Denning (test on the Master of Damage?).

29b7eca0-2660-5d04-adc2-06632123c2ec.alignment: cope's first wipe 0:18 to 0:55, OG Mesmer 1:12, wipes 2:29, 7:38, 8:40, end 9:11

claims.claim: Against a hex way, spike and run; against mirrors, spike in 40/40 sets to get as many off as we can; cold shields against the hex way (it turned out to be lightning).

check.evidence: Set choice per player is recorded (weapon sets); the engine does not yet compare spike rate by set.

claims.claim: Shell Shock between 'two' and 'one' of the countdown.

check.evidence: In this match OG's spikes with Cracked Armor on the target killed 6 of 16, without it 4 of 8; across 546 spikes in 61 matches, no difference (interval crosses zero).

claims.claim: The death penalty difference is hugely in our favour: cap the flag and spike them if they try to cap; advance slowly when they retreat.

check.evidence: cope had 18 deaths to OG's 1; the win model's top late contribution is the morale difference.

claims.claim: Migraine is not covered on me: I can't play, remove it.

check.evidence: Across 546 spikes in 61 matches, spikes with a hexed spiker killed 24% of the time against 41% without (interval 7 to 26 points). In this match most of OG's 24 spikes had 2 to 4 hexed spikers and 10 killed.

claims.claim: A spike-reducing skill (heard as 'Fainter harness') is nerfing our spike: throw on 'two' instead of 'one'.

check.evidence: The skill name is garbled in the transcript; landing spread for OG's spikes ranged 0.2 to 3.0 s.
